Permanent record ID: assertion.genebench.pro.provenance-wording-discrepancy.20261112

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge complexconstraints · dataset size: The ComplexConstraints v3 paper defines a seventy-five-prompt benchmark with 1,559 criteria and a disjoint one-thousand-prompt companion training set; both contain single-turn tasks with ten to forty criteria per prompt.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.complexconstraints.units.v2

  • The creator blog describes fifteen to forty rubric items, whereas the paper and README say ten to forty; these descriptions remain version-specific. Training and evaluation sets are manifestations of one family.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.10442.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Native speakers manually translate the prompt template, 79 attribute values and 36 scenarios into ten languages. Twenty-three models generate stories; a three-LLM ensemble extracts profiles covering nineteen demographic attributes.
  • The human harmfulness panel has 247 UK participants working in English and is 89.9% White. Participants rate 50 associations each, rather than validating every generated story.
  • The extraction audit covers 30 English/French stories. Extraction errors and nonuniform abstention can affect associations; the checked sample does not establish reliability in every language.
  • Pairwise co-occurrence does not decompose attribute mediation and is not interpreted causally; the human panel is one culturally bounded normative reference.
  • Main section 3 and Figure 10 ask harmful-stereotype agreement from strongly disagree to strongly agree; Appendix F.2 instead describes acceptability from not acceptable to fully acceptable. This wording/direction conflict remains unresolved.
  • Section 3 describes median rating aggregation, while section 4.3 and Figure 4 explicitly compare per-association mean human and mean model ratings over 1,580 associations. These are distinct stated summary scopes.
